video_title: Bitcoin Is Waiting On One Thing Before Institutions Go All-In
gist: iConnections CEO Ron Biscardi relays institutional LP sentiment: anxiety over a Texas data center slowdown after the midterms, a venture revival driven by the SpaceX IPO and expected Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin held back mainly by the lack of crypto regulation and bank custody, and private credit fears he calls overblown given low leverage and steady LP demand.

themes.theme: Midterms and the data center slowdown

insights.claim: Institutional allocators reacted to the midterm results with anxiety centered on AI, because they see data center construction as the engine of the stock market and any slowdown as handing China a competitive advantage.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Political risk to data center buildout is now the top AI-related worry among institutional LPs.
insights.quote: any slowing down of that of the construction of these facilities, it just gives China and frankly you know any any other country who wants to be competitive in this space a huge advantage over us

insights.claim: Texas, which holds roughly 13% of all planned US data centers, has an incoming Democratic governor-elect who has been open about wanting a data center moratorium, extending a slowdown already underway under the outgoing governor.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: A Texas pause hits a large share of the US data center pipeline.
insights.quote: I think something like 13% of all data centers planned in the United States just in the state of Texas.

insights.claim: Unpermitted data center projects in Texas will likely relocate to other states rather than wait 12 months, because in AI timelines a year-long delay is an eternity; already-permitted projects are hoped to proceed.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Watch for other states courting relocated data center projects; Texas permitting status becomes a key variable.
insights.quote: They're not going to they're not going to sit around for 12 months to wait and see what happens. I think that I think in AI years that's like an eternity.

insights.claim: Northern Virginia is the largest US data center cluster, and data center tax revenue there was large enough that some counties were able to lower real estate taxes.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Local fiscal benefits are a counter-argument to anti-data-center politics.

insights.claim: Biscardi argues Texas is the logical home for data centers because it combines the center of the US oil and gas industry (energy supply) with vast open land, so slowing builds there is illogical versus restricting them in metro areas.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Energy plus land availability is the core siting framework for AI infrastructure.

insights.claim: The market rallied strongly the day after the election, which Biscardi attributes primarily to the prospect of divided government.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Gridlock was read as market-positive despite AI policy anxiety.

insights.claim: SpaceX is betting a portion of the company on building and operating orbital data centers, framed as the natural response if terrestrial politics restrict data center construction.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Regulatory friction on Earth strengthens the case for space-based compute.

insights.claim: Biscardi contends latency is not a problem for orbital data centers, since an end-to-end SpaceX laser-linked network would require far fewer hops than the terrestrial cell system, as already demonstrated in Starlink.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Removes a commonly cited objection to orbital compute.
insights.quote: By the way, there's really not a latency issue. There's actually much more of a latency issue in the terrestrial.

insights.claim: If SpaceX gets orbital data centers working within about 3 years, it becomes a serious compute competitor, with Starship carrying roughly three Falcons' worth of satellites (around 100 per launch) and Falcon currently flying about 100-110 launches a year.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Starship cadence is the gating factor for SpaceX as a compute provider.
insights.quote: I think one Starship can put up the equivalent of like three Falcons worth of satellites.

insights.claim: Pompliano flags space traffic congestion as an underdiscussed issue that will become a big problem as orbital infrastructure scales.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Second-order risk for satellite-heavy business models.
insights.quote: there becomes a lot of space traffic, you know, which is something people don't yet talk about, but I think will become a big uh big issue.

themes.theme: Venture liquidity revival and AI lab valuations

insights.claim: Anthropic's expected IPO valuation has reportedly come down from about $2 trillion to around $1.5 trillion, and OpenAI's planned raise has reportedly shrunk from $30 billion to about $20 billion.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Signals some cooling in top-tier AI lab pricing.

insights.claim: Venture as an asset class struggled to raise money for three to four years because funds could not achieve liquidity, breaking the LP model of recycling distributions from funds one and two into funds three and four.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Liquidity, not returns on paper, governs LP appetite for illiquid assets.

insights.claim: At iConnections' late-February cap intro event venture funds struggled to get meetings, but by the June New York event they were the belle of the ball, a shift Biscardi ties to the SpaceX IPO.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: IPO exits rapidly reopen LP demand for venture.

insights.claim: SpaceX, about 20 years old, would have gone public roughly 15 years earlier in any prior era; companies now stay private longer due to public market changes and much larger private capital availability.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Late IPOs concentrate value creation in private markets.

insights.claim: Biscardi expects the Anthropic IPO to carry forward the venture momentum that started mid-year, and predicts venture will be a strong asset class for at least a few more years.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Supports continued LP allocation to tech venture.
insights.quote: my my guess is that venture is going to be a really strong asset class for at least a few more years.

insights.claim: Unlike the dot-com era of eyeballs without revenue, AI companies are huge revenue generators; Biscardi says Anthropic's revenue growth (roughly zero to $16 billion a year in four to five years) is unprecedented, though he doubts it should be worth $2 trillion.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Revenue reality complicates the AI bubble narrative, even if valuations are stretched.
insights.quote: Anthropics revenue growth is like nothing we have ever seen from any company in the history of business.

insights.claim: Institutional investors no longer view Bitcoin as snake oil and now see it as a legitimate asset class, a complete change from five or six years ago.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Legitimacy is no longer the barrier to institutional adoption.
insights.quote: I think people now see that it is a completely legitimate asset class.

insights.claim: Biscardi calls the Trump administration's failure to pass crypto regulation making it institutional grade a huge disappointment, and says regulation is the number one blocker to large institutional allocations.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Crypto market structure legislation is the key catalyst for institutional flows.
insights.quote: a huge disappointment, frankly, of the Trump administration has been the inability to get regulations passed to make it institutional grade.

insights.claim: If crypto regulatory infrastructure were established, Biscardi predicts a massive influx of institutional money and that the asset class would absolutely explode.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Regulatory passage is a binary upside catalyst.
insights.quote: if we could do it, I think the asset class would absolutely explode.

insights.claim: At iConnections events 50 to 100 crypto funds get many investor meetings, but Biscardi does not hear of billion-dollar checks; scaled crypto funds draw capital mostly from family offices and individuals rather than pensions, endowments and sovereign wealth funds.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Meetings are not converting to large allocations from the deepest pools of capital.

insights.claim: At iConnections' 2022 event, only 16 or 17 digital asset funds got 800 meetings among them, largely as investors used the meetings to educate themselves; the education gap has since largely closed.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: The adoption bottleneck has moved from education to regulation.

insights.claim: Big institutional crypto allocations require custody at firms like Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley or JPMorgan, and those banks will not enter in a big way until regulation is solved.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Bank custody is the sequencing step between regulation and institutional flows.
insights.quote: my assets are going to be custodied at Goldman Sachs or Morgan Stanley or JP Morgan.

insights.claim: The Binance hack is terrifying to institutions because there is no mainstream-market precedent for money being stolen from a major firm's accounts, whereas retail inflows to Binance exceeded outflows after the event because Binance backstopped the losses.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Retail and institutional reactions to exchange risk diverge sharply.
insights.quote: the inflows to Binance have been higher than the outflows postevent, which normally you wouldn't expect.

insights.claim: Biscardi calls private credit concerns totally overblown because funds run only about 2-3:1 leverage versus the 30-50:1 leverage at banks that created systemic risk in 2008.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Low leverage limits systemic contagion from private credit losses.
insights.quote: where you see real like systemic level blowups is when an asset class starts levering 30 to1, 40 to1, 50 to1

insights.claim: Private credit funds that lent too aggressively were mostly able to sell portfolios at 60 to 90 cents on the dollar, and the problems were confined to a handful of the biggest players rather than industry-wide.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Loss severity has been moderate, not a crash.

insights.claim: During the Blue Owl episode in Q1, private credit funds still had about 3,000 of roughly 20,000 meetings at iConnections' late-February Miami event, a top-three asset class, and the share of private credit funds signed up for the upcoming February event (about 700 funds total) is unchanged year over year.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: LP demand for private credit has not slowed despite headlines.

insights.claim: Private credit became a large part of portfolios because traditional bond portfolios could not generate returns in the zero-rate world, and it fills a middle-market lending void left by banks; new fund launches had become somewhat overheated and have slowed.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Structural demand underpins the asset class even as issuance cools.

insights.claim: Endowments, foundations and sovereign wealth funds have an effectively infinite time horizon, so once fixed income covers cash-flow needs they can ride out bad markets, making them slower to cool off or get excited than family offices and individuals.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Institutional flows lag sentiment shifts in both directions.
insights.quote: These big organizations have a a time horizon of infinity.

insights.claim: Analysts posting on X and Substack are now getting as much attention from public company CEOs as bank analysts, and in some cases more, prompting the Tomorrow Summit to give retail investors a bank-conference-style experience.
insights.speaker: Ron Biscardi
insights.so_what: Independent analysts are gaining access parity with sell-side research.
